stories.title: Why Indian law students don't want top judge at their graduation ceremony
stories.summary: India's top judges often make news for their rulings or pronunciations on weighty matters of law. But Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has recently made headlines for comments that have angered the youth and, in recent days, prompted students from two premier legal universities to demand that he should not be invited to be the chief guest at their convocations. The current row started on 23 July when dozens of outgoing students from Nalsar University of Law in the southern city of Hyderabad wrote an email to the college authorities asking that CJI Kant should not be invited to preside over their passing-out ceremony. The demand has since been supported by about 450 of the university's 1,400 students, including many juniors. The invitation to the chief justice is in keeping with tradition and for aspiring lawyers, the presence of the country's top judge at their convocation is usually seen as a matter of pride. But Nalsar students were upset over reports that a day earlier, the chief justice had turned down a request to hold urgent hearings on police brutality during the 20 July parliament march led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Delhi. Kant has since said he was misquoted. In fact, the CJP's birth was also rooted in a remark attributed to the chief justice amid reports that he had used terms like parasites and cockroaches to describe some youth. Kant had said he was misquoted then too. The crackdown against CJP protesters in the heart of the capital city, where police and paramilitaries were seen attacking and beating up unarmed students who were demanding education reforms with batons, wooden sticks and teargas, had shocked Indians and made global headlines. At least four youths had also sustained pellet gun injuries – in what was described as the first time such guns were used in the capital city for crowd control. Indian media reports, external said when a lawyer raised the matter before Kant on 22 July, the chief justice said, "don't waste our time" and when he was asked to watch videos of police excesses, he said "we don't have time".

stories.title: Pakistan top court orders Imran Khan’s hospital transfer amid access battle
stories.summary: Supreme Court grants jailed ex-PM Imran Khan transfer to hospital for nearly a month after concerns were raised over his blood pressure. Pakistan’s Supreme Court on Tuesday ordered the transfer of Imran Khan, former prime minister and founder of the opposition Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party, from Rawalpindi’s Adiala prison to Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital within two days, accepting a demand his party had been making for months. Uzair Bhandari, one of Khan’s lawyers, told Al Jazeera the three-member bench also ordered a medical board be formed to oversee Khan’s treatment, including the ex-prime minister’s sister, Dr Uzma Khan, and his personal physician, Dr Faisal Sultan. “The court also directed that Khan’s family be allowed to meet him at the hospital and that he be permitted to speak with his sons, who live abroad,” Bhandari said. The next hearing has been fixed for September 16, and Khan should remain hospitalised until at least then as per the order, according to the lawyer. This will be the longest period that Khan will be physically outside jail premises since he was imprisoned in August 2023, convicted in several corruption-related cases that he and his party insist are politically motivated. The order followed a report Adiala jail’s superintendent submitted to the court on Monday, detailing a cardiac board’s August 10 review of Khan, 73, which recorded fluctuating blood pressure and anxiety linked to restricted contact with his family. During Tuesday’s hearing, the court pressed Pakistan’s advocate general over gaps in the report, saying Khan’s “pulse and heart condition were not normal” and that his vital organs “had started being affected”. Courts had twice declined similar transfer requests since February, including an Islamabad High Court ruling that ordered a medical board’s assessment instead. Zulfi Bukhari, a senior PTI leader, told Al Jazeera the ruling reinforced the party’s longstanding position that Khan needed independent, specialised treatment outside Adiala jail. “Medical care provided within the prison system is no substitute for a thorough evaluation by independent specialists of his choosing,” he said, adding that PTI had consistently called for Khan’s transfer to Shifa International and access to his own doctors. Government officials have insisted any transfer required judicial authorisation rather than executive discretion.

stories.title: What we know about one of this year’s largest drone attacks on Moscow, Russian regions
stories.summary: In total, 791 Ukrainian UAVs were intercepted and destroyed over 16 Russian regions
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 18.
Last night’s Ukrainian drone attack on Russia was one of the largest since the start of 2026, calculations by TASS based on data from the Russian Defense Ministry indicate.
The attack resulted in a fatality, casualties and ground damage.
TASS has compiled key details about the attack’s impact.
Over the past night, as many as 791 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) were shot down or intercepted.

Namely, drones were intercepted and destroyed over the Belgorod, Bryansk, Vladimir, Volgograd, Voronezh, Kaluga, Kursk, Lipetsk, Oryol, Rostov, Ryazan, Tambov, Tula, Moscow, and Krasnodar Regions, the Republic of Crimea, the Sea of Azov, and the Black Sea.
An even larger attack was thwarted on Saturday night when Russia intercepted and destroyed 822 Ukrainian drones.
A previous large-scale attack was recorded on June 26 when 660 UAVs were downed across Russian regions.
On Monday night and Tuesday morning, air defenses and jamming systems repelled a major drone attack on the Moscow Region as more than 150 UAVs were shot down, according to Governor Andrey Vorobyev.
Air defense systems downed 65 Ukrainian UAVs over the Voronezh Region during the past night, with no casualties or damage reported, Governor Alexander Gusev said.
Air defenses destroyed 25 drones over the Kaluga Region, Governor Vladislav Shapsha wrote on Max channel.
More than 80 drones were destroyed in seven districts of southern Russia’s Rostov Region last night, Governor Yury Slyusar said.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz to remain closed until US fulfills memorandum terms — parliament speaker
stories.summary: In particular, Tehran demands that the blockade against Iran is lifted, frozen Iranian assets are unfrozen, the oil embargo is removed and threats and military operations on all fronts cease
article_sentences: "The Strait of Hormuz will not open until the blockade against Iran is lifted, frozen Iranian assets are unfrozen, the oil embargo is removed, threats and military operations on all fronts cease, and other conditions of the memorandum are fulfilled," Iran's Mehr news agency quoted him as saying.
The United States and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28.
In June, Washington and Tehran, mediated by Islamabad, signed a memorandum of understanding providing for an immediate halt to hostilities on all fronts, including in Lebanon.
However, the United States resumed large-scale strikes on Iran overnight into July 8, accusing it of violating the agreement's terms regarding the Strait of Hormuz.
